source_name: Pobjeda (pobjeda.me) — state-linked Montenegrin national daily
why_relevant: Confirmed as Montenegro's national daily newspaper (encyclopaedic reference surfaced in search). Historically state-owned/state-adjacent, which makes it the outlet most likely to carry official signing ceremonies, institutional contract announcements and government-side framing of contested tenders — complementary bias to Vijesti/Dan. Domain listed on strong prior, not on a returned article URL.

source_name: CdM — Cafe del Montenegro news portal
why_relevant: High-volume Montenegrin news portal named in the cell brief as a fast channel for business and procurement items. No article URL surfaced in my searches, so it is carried as an unverified prior rather than a confirmed find; its value is speed and breadth of economy coverage rather than depth.

source_name: RTCG — Radio and Television of Montenegro (public broadcaster)
why_relevant: Public service broadcaster confirmed to exist as Montenegro's national broadcaster; its news site is a standard carrier of institutional announcements including CBCG and ministry contract signings. Also itself a contracting authority. Domain not returned directly by search, so confidence reduced.

source_name: eKapija — regional business portal, Montenegro tender and procurement-plan sections
why_relevant: Commercial regional business-media aggregator that republishes and indexes tenders, procurement plans and company announcements including Montenegro, and covers commercial-company tenders that do not appear on state portals. Functions as a media-side pointer into both notices and the companies behind them.

source_name: SeeNews — Montenegro economy news
why_relevant: SEE business newswire covering Montenegrin payments infrastructure milestones in English, e.g. the CBCG licence agreement with the European Payments Council enabling the domestic instant payments scheme. Useful for English-language corroboration and for vendor/scheme naming around payment-system build-outs that precede procurement.

source_name: Montenegro Business / montenegrobusiness.eu
why_relevant: English-language Montenegro business outlet with analytical coverage of the July 2026 instant-payments introduction and its operational impact on banks — the demand-side context that drives bank technology procurement. Useful commentary channel, lower on primary fact origination.

source_name: monte.business — Montenegro Business (English news site)
why_relevant: Reported Montenegro signing an agreement for a real-time instant payment system with Italy's central bank — a concrete cross-border technology/service arrangement of exactly the kind rarely visible in national notice portals. Note this domain is distinct from montenegrobusiness.eu despite similar branding; treat provenance carefully.

source_name: The Fintech Times — Montenegro fintech ecosystem coverage
why_relevant: International fintech trade press with a dedicated 2026 Montenegro ecosystem piece. Useful for identifying vendors, fintech entrants and partnership deals that local media may not name, and as an actor-map feeder for the cell.

source_name: Bloomberg Adria (regional business media, HR/SI/RS editions)
why_relevant: Regional Adria business media producing analytical pieces on enterprise software purchases and digital transformation ('Kupili smo softver – gdje je transformacija?') and a standing digitalizacija desk. Relevant as regional commentary that frames bank IT spending and occasionally names vendors and deal sizes across the Adria region including Montenegro.

source_name: Sandžak Press — regional Balkan news portal covering Montenegro procurement disputes
why_relevant: Concrete worked example of the exact story type this cell targets: a partially annulled tender for ANPR/OCR equipment and software after a rights-protection complaint alleging tailored, competition-limiting documentation. Demonstrates that regional portals republish Montenegrin procurement-dispute reporting and are therefore a usable redundancy channel when the originating outlet is paywalled or offline.

source_name: Antena M (antenam.net) — independent Podgorica radio and news portal
why_relevant: Independent Podgorica-based broadcaster confirmed to exist and operate antenam.net. Known for combative political and accountability coverage, so a plausible carrier of procurement-affair reporting, but no procurement article surfaced in this run — carried as a low-confidence monitoring candidate.

source_name: Crnogorski Telekom tender page (corporate, media-adjacent disclosure)
why_relevant: Surfaced repeatedly alongside procurement press coverage: a private/majority-foreign-owned operator publishing its own tenders outside the state portal. Directly demonstrates the pattern this cell cares about — non-state buyers of ICT publishing procurement on their own sites, which media then report. A template for checking whether Montenegrin banks do the same.

source_name: EPCG (Elektroprivreda Crne Gore) public procurement page
why_relevant: State utility publishing its own javne nabavke; recurred in procurement-affair searches. Not banking, but it is one of the largest Montenegrin buyers of IT/metering/payment-adjacent systems and a frequent subject of media procurement controversy, making it a useful comparator and a source of vendor names active in the same market as bank IT suppliers.

source_name: Udruženje banaka Crne Gore (UBCG) – Association of Montenegrin Banks
why_relevant: Sector association whose member list enumerates the full bank population (reported as 11 member banks) — the buyer universe for A2 tenders. Also publishes the 'Bankar' magazine, event announcements and conference programmes that name technology vendors before contracts surface as notices.

source_name: INFINTECH – Western Balkans banking & fintech conference (organised by Logate)
why_relevant: Annual Montenegro-hosted banking/fintech conference (Porto Montenegro; next edition announced 8-9 Oct 2026). Its sponsor and agenda pages name exactly which payment/core-banking vendors are courting which Montenegrin banks — a pre-tender signal. Past sponsors observed in reporting include Mastercard, CRIF, GD Next, Poslovna inteligencija, plus Hipotekarna banka, Erste Bank Montenegro and NLB Banka Podgorica as participating banks.

source_name: Logate d.o.o. (Podgorica) – corporate site / customer references
why_relevant: Montenegrin banking-software house and INFINTECH organiser. Its references/news and whitepapers (e.g. 'Digital Banking Universe') reveal which local banks it implements for — direct evidence of awarded but rarely-noticed private-sector contracts.

source_name: Payten (ASEE Group) – Montenegro operations page
why_relevant: Incumbent ATM/POS service provider in Montenegro; public statements cite six service centres and installed-base figures (500+ ATMs, 13,000+ POS delivered; 350+ ATMs and 7,000+ POS maintained). Installed-base and service-centre disclosures are the strongest weak signal for upcoming refresh/maintenance tenders and for competitor share.

source_name: Montenegrin Foreign Investors Council (MFIC) – list of members
why_relevant: Enumerates foreign-owned companies active in Montenegro, including banks and payment/IT vendors (Payten confirmed as a member). Each member profile is a short company dossier — useful for building the vendor/actor map and for spotting new market entrants.

source_name: ICT Cortex – Montenegrin IT cluster, member companies
why_relevant: IT cluster whose member list is the best single enumeration of Montenegrin software/integrator firms capable of bidding on banking IT tenders (Logate and peers). Doubles as a pointer to member news and hiring.

source_name: Privredna komora Crne Gore (Chamber of Economy) – ICT board and member directory
why_relevant: Statutory chamber with sectoral boards (odbor udruženja za IKT, odbor za bankarstvo i finansije) and a company directory; its board minutes and event announcements name vendor and bank participants. Classic pointer source for actor discovery in a small market.

source_name: Zaposli.me – Montenegro job portal, IT category
why_relevant: Largest Montenegrin job board. Bank vacancies for implementation, integration and vendor-management roles frequently name the platform being introduced (core banking, card management, AML) months before any award notice appears.

source_name: posao.crna.gora.me – job ads + company directory (adresar preduzeća)
why_relevant: Job portal combined with a Montenegrin company directory and business magazine — serves both as a hiring-signal feed and as a pointer source for enumerating vendors. Has dedicated position pages such as 'IT menadžer/ka'.

source_name: Pazar3.me – classifieds, IT jobs section
why_relevant: High-volume Montenegrin classifieds site carrying IT vacancies (programmers, project managers, DBAs) including from banks and their integrators; complements the formal job boards and catches smaller vendors that do not post elsewhere.
